title: Three painters
prompt:
Three painters can each paint a hall alone in 8, 12 and 24 hours. Each works at a steady pace.

How many hours will they take to paint the hall if all three work together?
hints: If one painter working alone needs a given number of hours for the whole hall, what fraction of the hall does it do in one hour?
When all three painters work at once, how do the fractions of the hall done in an hour combine?
If that combined fraction is done every hour, how many hours does the whole hall take?
solution:
**4 hours.**

Think in fractions of the hall per hour. Working alone, the painters do 1/8, 1/12 and 1/24 of the hall in one hour. Working together, their rates add: 1/8 + 1/12 + 1/24 = 6/24 = 1/4 of the hall per hour.

If 1/4 of the hall is done each hour, the whole hall takes **4** hours with all three painters at work.

The common slip is adding or averaging the times. Times do not add, but rates do.
